draft.title: Corporate social responsibility in change
card: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) is a business's duty to act ethically and consider the effects of its decisions on people and the environment, not only on profit.
When a business makes a change, such as closing a site or adopting new technology, CSR asks who is affected and how.
a socially responsible change treats employees fairly, for example by giving early notice, offering retraining or helping those who lose their jobs.
the business also considers local people and nature, for example by limiting pollution or waste and by supporting a town that relied on its jobs.
draft.remember: A responsible change counts the effects on staff, the community and the environment, as well as profit.

a.q: Which action shows a business applying CSR when it makes a change?
opts: Retraining staff whose jobs are replaced by new machines
Choosing the cheapest change, whatever its effects on others
Telling staff about the change only after it has started
Making the change only where it lifts profit the most
a.why: Retraining staff weighs the effect of the change on the people it affects, not just the cost. The other options focus on cost or profit alone, or give staff no say.
a.clue: Which option cares about the people affected, not only the money?

b.q: Harlow Foods in Ballarat plans to move its packing to a cheaper site in another state. Which plan is the most socially responsible?
opts: Give 6 months notice, offer job help and fund local training
Keep the move secret to avoid upset, then pay the minimum
Move fast to save money, since profit is the main aim
Offer a pay rise if staff promise not to talk to the media
b.why: Early notice, job help and local support consider staff and the community as well as cost. Paying only the legal minimum or buying silence still puts the business's interests first, so neither is the most responsible plan.
b.clue: Look for the plan that cares about staff and the town, not just the business.

a.best: Retraining staff whose jobs are replaced by new machines

b.best: Give 6 months notice, offer job help and fund local training

Keep the move secret, pay out staff, fund town training
